intent: Revert to the iteration 1 and 4 reference geometry: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m with y = 0.05 m, and unchanged wheel, body and mass values. I changed the span back from ±0.04 m because iteration 5 lowered the score and progress. Expected result: score near 69.3, with line_loss_events about 1 per run and progress about 0.17 mean. I am considering, without committing, a later single test of a different body or wheel parameter, but only after the controller is held fixed, because the current evidence is confounded by controller changes.
learning: The span has now been tested at ±0.024 (54.37 with a controller change), ±0.03 (69.32, the best), and ±0.04 (52.47). ±0.03 m is the best measured span at 12 mm and y=0.05 m. The 16 mm footprint and y=0.03 m both lowered the score. Line loss has stayed near 1 per run under every geometry, so the next lever is probably the controller's line-loss handling, not the sensor layout. Next iteration: if the score returns to about 69 with this geometry, hold it and let the Integrator work on the controller.
rationale: Iteration 5 widened the span to ±0.04 m (20 mm spacing, 12 mm footprints, y=0.05 m) and scored 52.47, down 16.9 points from the 69.32 reference. Line loss fell on oval (1.65 to 1.0 per run) but stayed at 1.0 on s-bend and slalom, so it did not fall clearly below 1 per run. Oval progress roughly halved (0.254 to 0.127), and mean progress fell on every track except s-bend, which was roughly flat (0.150 to 0.150). The Integrator's rule applies: because the score and progress fell with ±0.04 m, revert to the ±0.03 m span at y=0.05 m. I took that advice. Iterations 1 and 4 used this exact geometry and both scored 69.3241, so this is the best-measured design. I am not testing any new geometry this iteration: wheel track, wheel radius, mass and body have no evidence pointing to them, and the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m because body width does not move it. The expected result is a score near 69 if the controller is unchanged, and a return to the reference if the controller changes.
